roles.label: Strategy pattern role diagram
roles.description: Context holds exactly one Strategy and offers contextInterface() and setStrategy(strategy). Strategy declares algorithmInterface(). ConcreteStrategy implements Strategy. A Client creates a ConcreteStrategy and configures the Context with it.
roles.caption: A hollow diamond with an arrow means Context has a Strategy; a dashed arrow with a hollow triangle means ConcreteStrategy implements Strategy. The Client is not a role of the pattern, but it makes the choice.

solution.label: Strategy solution structure
solution.description: Expense holds its total, its people, and one SplitStrategy, and forwards shares() and label() to it. EqualSplit, PercentSplit, and BirthdaySplit each implement SplitStrategy. PercentSplit keeps its percentages, BirthdaySplit keeps its guest and reuses EqualSplit. Expense does not depend on the concrete strategies.
solution.caption: Expense plays Context; SplitStrategy plays Strategy; EqualSplit, PercentSplit, and BirthdaySplit play Concrete Strategy. The Context depends only on the Strategy interface.

sequence.label: Sequence of the traced requests
sequence.description: The app asks dinner for its shares, and dinner forwards split(total, people) to the shared EqualSplit object. The app calls setStrategy(percent) on dinner and asks for the shares again; dinner forwards split(total, people) to the PercentSplit object. The app asks dinner for its label, and dinner forwards label() to the PercentSplit object.
sequence.caption: Each request goes to whichever strategy the expense holds. The messages appear as the narration reaches them; the panel below shows each result.
sequence.source:
@startuml
participant app
participant dinner: Expense
participant equal as : EqualSplit
participant percent as : PercentSplit
steps:
app -> dinner: shares()
activate dinner
dinner -> equal: split(total, people)
activate equal
deactivate equal
deactivate dinner
app -> dinner: setStrategy(percent)
app -> dinner: shares()
activate dinner
dinner -> percent: split(total, people)
activate percent
deactivate percent
deactivate dinner
app -> dinner: label()
activate dinner
dinner -> percent: label()
activate percent
deactivate percent
deactivate dinner

cards.title: Benefit: a family of algorithms
cards.text: Each algorithm and its data live in one class; adding one leaves the Context and the others untouched, and the conditionals disappear.

cards.title: Benefit: an alternative to subclassing
cards.text: The Context stays one class; clients switch algorithms at runtime, and each strategy can be tested alone.

cards.title: Liability: informed clients, more objects
cards.text: Clients must know how strategies differ; every algorithm adds a class, and one interface serves them all.

cards.title: A good fit
cards.text: Several interchangeable algorithms for one task, chosen by clients, with more on the way.

cards.title: Simpler alternatives
cards.text: Two stable variants — a conditional. One stateless operation — pass a function.

cards.title: Not State, not Template Method
cards.text: A client chooses a Strategy; State objects replace one another; Template Method varies steps through subclasses.

cards.title: Itemized
cards.text: Each friend pays for the dishes they ordered.

cards.title: Tax and tip
cards.text: Shared in proportion to each friend's dishes.

cards.title: Your task
cards.text: Name the class you add and every existing line that changes.

cards.title: Context
cards.text: One task can be done by a family of interchangeable algorithms, clients choose among them, and new ones keep arriving.

cards.title: Problem
cards.text: Hard-wiring the algorithms into one class, in conditionals or subclasses, scatters each algorithm and blocks switching at runtime.

cards.title: Solution
cards.text: A Context delegates to a Strategy interface; each Concrete Strategy implements one algorithm, and the client chooses which one the Context holds.

cards.title: Consequences
cards.text: Interchangeable, independently testable algorithms without conditionals, at the cost of informed clients, more objects, and one shared interface.
